Higher resolution increases the number of gradient terms in the sum [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the integral for TV regularization is discretized by dividing the interval into regular grids. The resulting formula is a triple summation from i=1 to N, j=1 to N, and k=1 to N. In this context, N represents the resolution (number of grid points per dimension). Therefore, increasing the resolution (increasing N) directly increases the number of terms in the summation (from N^3 to a larger number).

Unlike Anisotropic Total Variation (ATV), which sums the absolute values of individual gradient components, ITV sums the Euclidean magnitude of the full 3D gradient vector at each voxel, treating the gradient components as a coupled group [S3, unofficial][S4, unofficial].

The claim states that unlike Anisotropic Total Variation (ATV), which sums absolute values of individual gradient components, Isotropic Total Variation (ITV) sums the Euclidean magnitude of the full 3D gradient vector, treating components as a coupled group. Source [S4] explicitly defines ATV as summing the absolute values of individual gradient components (Eq 4.6) and defines ITV as summing the magnitudes of the gradient vectors (Eq 4.2.3), which corresponds to the L2 norm of the gradient vector components. Source [S3] notes confirm that ITV uses GroupL1Norm to treat gradient components as a group, enforcing isotropy. Thus, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.

The ITV prior $h(\mathbf{x})$ is defined as the sum of the $L_2$ norms of the gradient vectors at all voxels [S4, unofficial][S5, unofficial]:

The claim states that the ITV prior $h( oldsymbol{x})$ is defined as the sum of the $L_2$ norms of the gradient vectors at all voxels. Source [S4] explicitly defines the ITV prior as $h(x) = sum_{ijk} sqrt{|x_{i+1,j,k} - x_{i,j,k}|^2 + |x_{i,j+1,k} - x_{i,j,k}|^2 + |x_{i,j,k+1} - x_{i,j,k}|^2}$, which corresponds to the sum of the magnitudes (L2 norms) of the 3-element gradient vectors $w^v$ at each voxel. It further clarifies that $||w||_E = sum_v ||w^v||_2$. Source [S5] provides the identical definition and formula. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.

Useful in sparse-view CT and differentiable volume rendering to prevent overfitting [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the technique is useful in sparse-view CT and differentiable volume rendering to prevent overfitting. Source [S1] explicitly mentions that regularization via TV norm leads to high-quality reconstructions in differentiable rendering methods and discusses how trilinear interpolation prevents overfitting observed in Siddon's method (a differentiable volume rendering technique). It also notes that Siddon's method exactly computes line integrals, which is relevant to sparse-view scenarios where exact path computation is critical. Source [S3] provides code for sparse-view CT (1000 angles, fan beam geometry) using Total Variation (TV) regularization (GroupL1Norm), which is a standard technique to prevent overfitting in ill-posed inverse problems like sparse-view CT. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
